questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Quantum Radial Nodes & Probability Density
questions.question: For the $3d_{z^2}$ atomic orbital of a hydrogen-like atom in [Atomic Structure], what are the numbers of radial nodes and angular nodes respectively?
questions.solution: For a $3d$ orbital: principal quantum number $n = 3$, azimuthal quantum number $l = 2$. Radial nodes $= n - l - 1 = 3 - 2 - 1 = 0$. Angular nodes $= l = 2$ (conical nodal surfaces).
questions.explanation: Analyze using fundamental chemical principles in Atomic Structure.

questions.topic: Quantum Radial Nodes & Probability Density
questions.question: What is the basicity (number of ionizable hydrogen atoms per molecule) of pyrophosphoric acid $(\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7)$ in [Atomic Structure]?
questions.solution: Pyrophosphoric acid contains two tetrahedral phosphorus atoms connected by a $\text{P-O-P}$ bridge, with four $-\text{OH}$ groups attached directly to phosphorus. All four hydrogens are acidic, so its basicity is $4$.
questions.explanation: Calculate using quantitative laws in Atomic Structure.
